title: The Red Star Upstairs  (楼上的红星标记)

segments.t: 汉娜、格雷厄姆和凯勒布各自端着盛有冠军浆果杏仁蛋糕的盘子，走到庭院遮阴的大树下，一边对照着四张拼起来的卡片地图，一边抬头望向二楼的木阳台。先听一遍他们的对话。
Stand right beside table one and match the four card drawing to our upstairs wall.
There is the wooden balcony outside the second floor landing — right where the red star sits!
Squint under the left corner beam of that balcony railing, Caleb; what do you see?
Hold on — there is a forged iron ring bolted straight into the heavy oak post!
And look at the trunk of our courtyard shade tree — a matching ring high up!
Now the mapmaker's note makes total sense: they strung festival lanterns overhead between those rings!
High roof to tree lanterns shining down over all twenty-eight seats on Saturday night!
Wait — have you checked the weekend weather forecast for Friday and Saturday afternoon, Graham?
Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
Paper lanterns plus strong afternoon wind? That sounds like an adventure waiting to happen!
Then Friday morning we climb onto that balcony with sturdy cord and test every knot!
Bring my wooden ladder at nine sharp — this courtyard is going to glow like daylight!
现在让我们顺着他们的目光一起望向阳台，逐句解析。
Stand right beside table one and match the four card drawing to our upstairs wall.
“就站在一号桌旁边，把那张四合一卡片上的图和我们楼上的墙面对应起来看。”凯勒布像个专业建筑师一样指挥站位：
Stand right beside table one
stand 表示“站立、站到某处”；table one 前面不加冠词，直接用作专有编号。
match the four card drawing to our upstairs wall.
match something to something 意思是“把……和……对应起来”；upstairs 在名词 wall 前作定语，表示“楼上的”。
There is the wooden balcony outside the second floor landing — right where the red star sits!
“二楼楼梯平台外侧就是那个木阳台——正好就是那颗红星标着的位置！”汉娜立刻找到了对应点：
outside the second floor landing
这里的 landing 不是“降落”，而是指楼梯间的“楼梯平台”。另外，在美国，second floor 指的是地面一层往上的“二楼”。
right where the red star sits!
用来描述物体所在的位置时，英语常用 sit（位于、在那里）。
Squint under the left corner beam of that balcony railing, Caleb; what do you see?
“凯勒布，眯起眼睛往那道阳台栏杆左角那根横梁底下看；你看见什么了？”格雷厄姆指向一个隐蔽的细节：
Squint under the left corner beam
squint 一个词就把“眯起眼睛看”全概括了。beam 可以指建筑的“横梁”，也可以指“光线”。
what do you see?
在一般现在时里提出问题，要借助助动词 do。
Hold on — there is a forged iron ring bolted straight into the heavy oak post!
“等一下——那根粗重的橡木柱上直接用螺栓固定着一个锻铁环！”凯勒布发现了意想不到的物件：
Hold on
Hold on 是口语里常用的“等一下、先别动”，打电话时也经常听到。
a forged iron ring bolted
forged 是“锻造的”（不过 forge 也有“伪造”的意思）。bolted 来自名词 bolt（螺栓），指“用螺栓拧紧固定的”。
And look at the trunk of our courtyard shade tree — a matching ring high up!
“快看我们庭院遮阴大树的树干——高处也有一个一模一样的铁环！”汉娜找到了另一头配对的铁环：
the trunk of our courtyard shade tree
trunk 是“树干”，在美式英语里还指汽车的“后备箱”。shade 指乘凉的“树荫”，而 shadow 通常指物体的“影子、轮廓”。
a matching ring high up!
matching 来自 match，意思是“相配的、成对的、一模一样的”。
Now the mapmaker's note makes total sense: they strung festival lanterns overhead between those rings!
“现在制图师的笔记完全说得通了：他们当年就在那些铁环之间的头顶上方挂了一串节日灯笼！”格雷厄姆终于明白原计划是怎么回事了：
makes total sense:
英语表达“说得通、有道理”固定用动词 make：make sense，不能说 have sense。
they strung festival lanterns overhead
strung 是 string（用绳串起、悬挂）的不规则过去式；overhead 表示“在头顶上方”。
High roof to tree lanterns shining down over all twenty-eight seats on Saturday night!
“从高高的屋檐一直挂到大树的灯笼，星期六晚上照亮下面所有的二十八个座位！”汉娜已经开始畅想周年庆晚宴了：
shining down over all twenty-eight seats
down 加上了光线从上往下照的方向感；twenty-eight 中间要加连字符。
on Saturday night!
在具体的星期几前面用介词 on，不加冠词（on Saturday night）。
Wait — have you checked the weekend weather forecast for Friday and Saturday afternoon, Graham?
“等等——格雷厄姆，你查过星期五和星期六下午的周末天气预报了吗？”凯勒布谨慎地想到了天气问题：
have you checked
这里用现在完成时（have you checked）来询问某件事是否已经办妥，不强调具体时间点。
the weekend weather forecast
注意别把 weather（天气）和 whether（是否）弄混了：这两个词读音完全相同。
Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
“天空晴朗，傍晚温暖，星期五还会有一阵阵清冽的春风吹过全城。”格雷厄姆像天气预报员一样念了出来：
Clear skies, warm evenings,
evening 指下午快结束、天色渐暗到入夜前的“傍晚”。
brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town
gust 指“一阵强风”；brisk 形容风“清冽劲爽的”；sweep across 意思是“横扫、吹过”。
Paper lanterns plus strong afternoon wind? That sounds like an adventure waiting to happen!
“纸灯笼遇上大风的下午？这听起来简直是注定要出事的冒险！”汉娜幽默地预感到了麻烦：
That sounds like
sound like 后面接名词，表示“听起来像……”。
an adventure waiting to happen!
waiting to happen 形容某种几乎必然会发生的事；日常很常见 a disaster waiting to happen（早晚要出事的隐患）。
Then Friday morning we climb onto that balcony with sturdy cord and test every knot!
“那么星期五早上我们就带上结实的绳索爬上那个阳台，逐一检查每个绳结！”凯勒布提出了务实的解决办法；sturdy 意思是“结实的、坚固的”：
we climb onto that balcony
climb onto 表示“爬到……上面”；注意 climb 结尾的字母 b 不发音。
test every knot!
knot 开头的 k 同样不发音，所以它和 not 读音完全一样。
Bring my wooden ladder at nine sharp — this courtyard is going to glow like daylight!
“九点整把我的木梯拿过来——这个庭院会亮得像白昼一样！”格雷厄姆充满干劲地为这一集收了尾：
at nine sharp
在具体钟点后面加上 sharp，意思是“……点整”。ladder 指可移动的“梯子”，建筑里的固定楼梯则叫 stairs。
is going to glow like daylight!
is going to 预示着即将成真的未来景象；glow 指柔和温暖的光芒。最后，请按正常语速再完整听一遍这一幕。
Stand right beside table one and match the four card drawing to our upstairs wall.
There is the wooden balcony outside the second floor landing — right where the red star sits!
Squint under the left corner beam of that balcony railing, Caleb; what do you see?
Hold on — there is a forged iron ring bolted straight into the heavy oak post!
And look at the trunk of our courtyard shade tree — a matching ring high up!
Now the mapmaker's note makes total sense: they strung festival lanterns overhead between those rings!
High roof to tree lanterns shining down over all twenty-eight seats on Saturday night!
Wait — have you checked the weekend weather forecast for Friday and Saturday afternoon, Graham?
Clear skies, warm evenings, and brisk spring wind gusts sweeping across town on Friday.
Paper lanterns plus strong afternoon wind? That sounds like an adventure waiting to happen!
Then Friday morning we climb onto that balcony with sturdy cord and test every knot!
Bring my wooden ladder at nine sharp — this courtyard is going to glow like daylight!
尘封三十年的蛋糕食谱终于补全，所有人的目光如今都投向了二楼阳台——以及星期五即将刮起的大风！第三集到此结束——我们第四集见！
See you next time!
